glance: Sweet shops in Feni town and Parshuram
khondoler-mishti.desc: Khondoler mishti is a soft chhana sweet in the rosogolla family, soaked in syrup, that originated in the Khondol area of Parshuram upazila. It is known for its fine texture and has become Feni's best-known gift for visitors. Sweet shops in Feni town and Parshuram sell it fresh daily.

glance: 160 km to Feni by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
chandgazi-bhuiyan-mosque.desc: This old mosque in Chhagalnaiya upazila is one of several Mughal-period mosques in Feni district. It has the compact, domed form typical of mosques of that era. Village surroundings and very few visitors make it a quiet detour for those interested in architecture.
blocks: How to get there
From Feni town take a CNG toward Chhagalnaiya and ask locally for the mosque.
Good to know
It is an active mosque; avoid prayer times and dress modestly.

glance: 160 km to Feni by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
bijoy-singh-dighi.desc: Bijoy Singh Dighi is one of the biggest old ponds in the region, its broad surface ringed with trees and paths. Local tradition links its name to a historic ruler, though stories vary. Today it is a calm place where people walk, fish and sit by the water. The nearby highway makes it an easy break on a road trip.
blocks: How to get there
A short CNG ride west of Feni town, near the Dhaka–Chattogram highway.
Good to know
Late afternoon is pleasant. Keep to the paths.

bhasha-shaheed-salam-memorial.desc: Abdus Salam, one of the martyrs shot in Dhaka on 21 February 1952 while protesting for Bangla as a state language, was born in a village of Daganbhuiyan upazila in Feni. The village, now renamed Salamnagar, has a memorial library and museum in his honour. Visiting on or around 21 February, International Mother Language Day, shows how deeply the movement is remembered locally.
blocks: Good to know
On 21 February, join locals laying flowers early in the morning; dress respectfully.

glance: 160 km to Feni by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
muhuri-project.desc: The Muhuri Project, built to irrigate and protect farmland, has a closure dam near where the Feni, Muhuri and other rivers meet the coast. Behind the dam a wide lake forms in the dry season, with fish farms, planted forest and open sky all around. In winter, ducks and other migratory birds gather on the water, and boatmen offer short rides. The site also had Bangladesh's first wind power station.
blocks: How to get there
About 25 km from Feni town via Sonagazi; take a bus or CNG.
Good to know
Bring binoculars in winter. Agree boat fares before setting out and keep clear of the sluice gates.

glance: 160 km to Feni by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
rajajhir-dighi.desc: Rajajhir Dighi, the 'king's daughter's pond', lies at the centre of Feni town, surrounded by government offices and walkways. Local legend says it was dug for a raja's daughter. Its banks are a gathering place for townspeople in the evenings.
blocks: How to get there
In central Feni town, walkable or by rickshaw.
Good to know
Combine with a sweet-shop stop in town.

glance: 160 km to Feni by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
shamsher-gazi-fort.desc: Shamsher Gazi (1712–1760) rose from a local strongman to rule Roshnabad and much of Tripura in the mid-18th century, and folk memory calls him the 'Tiger of Bhati'. At Champaknagar and Jagannath Sonapur in Chhagalnaiya, right on the Indian border, are places linked to him: a large tank, the remains of a tunnel and the site of his fort, though the fort itself has vanished and part of his capital lies across the border in Tripura. A small tourist centre called Shamsher Gazi's Bansher Kella (bamboo fort) has been built here to keep the story alive. It makes a pleasant half-day out from Feni.
blocks: How to get there
From Feni town take a bus or CNG to Chhagalnaiya, then a CNG to Champaknagar/Jagannath Sonapur.
Good to know
This is right on the border; carry ID and follow BGB instructions. Check the resort's opening hours if you plan to eat there.

glance: 160 km to Feni by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
shilua-stone.desc: In Madhya Shilua village of Pathannagar union, Chhagalnaiya, stands an old stone block that gave the village its name. Marks on it have been read as early Brahmi script, and remains of stone images found nearby suggest an ancient Buddhist or Hindu site. Locals call it the 'shil ghar'; in British times it had a canopy and railings, now gone, and one local legend says it fell from the sky. The inscription is protected under the antiquities law, but very few outsiders come.
blocks: How to get there
From Feni go toward Chhagalnaiya to Contractor Masjid Bazar (about 12–13 km), then about 3 km south to Shilua Chowdhury Bazar; the stone is a short walk west of the bazar.
Good to know
Ask locals for 'Shiluar shil'. Do not touch or chip the stone.

glance: 160 km to Feni by road, 4–6 hours by bus or car
sat-math-chhagalnaiya.desc: In West Chhagalnaiya, on Satbari Road, lies the eight-acre estate of the Hindu zamindar Binod Bihari. Beside the house stand seven memorial (cremation) temples, which is why the place is called Sat Math or Sat Mandir Bari. The zamindar left for Kolkata around 1948, and local families now live in the old buildings. It is listed by the Department of Archaeology but is almost unknown outside Feni.
blocks: How to get there
From Feni take a bus or CNG to Chhagalnaiya town, then a rickshaw to Satbari Road in West Chhagalnaiya.
Good to know
People live in the compound; ask before photographing homes.

glance: Markets in Sonagazi and Feni town
sonagazi-char-doi.desc: Buffaloes graze on the low coastal islands of Sonagazi, and their rich milk is set into curd in round clay pots. It is denser and more sour than ordinary sweet doi, often eaten after a meal or with puffed rice and molasses. Local markets sell it by the pot.
